title: Airline to Charge Passengers to Use Overhead Lockers
paragraphs: Years ago, passengers traveling by plane just had to pay for their airline ticket, and rarely had to pay hidden costs.
These days, it feels like airlines are finding ways to charge passengers for everything — bags, in-flight entertainment, food.
And now, one airline has announced that it will start charging passengers to use space in the overhead compartments!

Passengers traveling with Australian airline Jetstar are currently allowed to bring a 7-kilogram bag with them on the plane. This bag is often weighed at the gate by airline staff before boarding, and can then be stowed under the seat or in the overhead compartment.
But the carrier has announced that it is scrapping this system, and passengers will only be able to stow their bags under the seat in front of them free of charge.
From February 2027, the airline will introduce the option to pay for space in the overhead compartment for bag storage.

The move comes after passengers and airline staff named "having bags weighed at the gate and struggling to find room in overhead lockers as the more stressful parts of the airport experience," Jetstar said.

The cost of using the overhead compartments will start from $18 one way, with the price depending on the route. Bags stowed in the compartments can weigh up to 10 kilograms, but they will not be weighed before boarding.
Jetstar said the change would reduce frustrations at boarding gates, ensure customers only pay for what they need, and help more flights leave on time.
But this move has not reduced all frustration — many people online have said they don't agree with the change.
"What next? A fee to use the toilet?" one person wrote.
However, others have supported the change, with many saying they're often left with no space to even stow their jacket because people's bags take up so much room.
